podcast.title: TV Debut on The Andy Williams Show (1963)
podcast.body: Donnie Osmond made his television debut at the age of four on "The Andy Williams Show" in 1963, endearing himself to audiences as "cute as a bug." "Four-year-old Donnie Osman who was cute as a bug Made his TV debut on the Andy Williams show in 1963."

srcs.episode: Ep. 27 - That's Entertainment! TV Variety Shows of the 70s

podcast.title: Image on Tiger Beat Magazine (1970)
podcast.body: Donnie Osmond, at ten years old, appeared on the October 1970 cover of *Tiger Beat* magazine alongside David Cassidy and Bobby Sherman, featured with a caption that some found "creepy." "Ten-year-old Donnie is pointing at the camera looking cute as a bug and the caption is, spend the night with us. What? Ew. Spend the night with ten-year-old Donnie..."

srcs.episode: Ep. 30 - The Sweet Sound of 70s Bubblegum Music

podcast.title: Teen Heartthrob Status (1973)
podcast.body: By 1973, Donnie Osmond had become a significant teen heartthrob, a status that was a key factor in his becoming the lead singer of The Osmonds, not just for his voice, but for his ability to elicit enthusiastic reactions from female fans. "Ten years later Donnie was a teen heartthrob But he and his brothers had to get rid of that Andy Williams image."

srcs.episode: Ep. 27 - That's Entertainment! TV Variety Shows of the 70s

podcast.title: The Donnie & Marie Show (1975-1979)
podcast.body: Donnie and his younger sister Marie parlayed their immense popularity into a highly successful variety show, "The Donnie & Marie Show," which aired from 1975 to 1979. Its success was surprising given the general decline in variety show popularity by 1975. "This one was on from 1975 to 1979 The thing about this show is that by 1975 variety shows were declining in popularity So nobody other than adolescent girls like me, the proud owner of Donnie and Marie Barbies saw that success coming."

podcast.title: Las Vegas Residency (2008-2019)
podcast.body: Donnie and Marie Osmond enjoyed an unexpected 11-year run with their show in Las Vegas, which concluded in November 2019, when Donnie was 61 and Marie was 60. "Surely they did not think that 40 years later they would have another 11 year run with their show in Las Vegas But they did, it came to an end in November 2019 when 61 year old Donnie and 60 year old Marie closed out their last show in Las Vegas."

podcast.title: "I'm a Little Bit Country, I'm a Little Bit Rock and Roll" Skit
podcast.body: On "The Donnie & Marie Show," the siblings performed a popular weekly skit based on the song "I'm a Little Bit Country, I'm a Little Bit Rock and Roll," with Marie representing country and Donnie representing rock and roll. Country singer Mark Cooper adjusted the lyrics for their brother-sister dynamic. "Every week they did a skit based on I'm a little bit country, I'm a little bit rock and roll with Marie being the country and Donnie being the rock and roll."

podcast.title: 70s Teen Idol Hit Remakes
podcast.body: Donny Osmond was one of several 1970s teen idols who found chart success through hit remakes, demonstrating that covers provided an "easy way" for such pin-ups to enter the charts. "There were hit remakes by such pin-ups as Donnie Osmond"

podcast.title: Cause of Fan Hysteria
podcast.body: Donnie Osmond was the primary reason for the screaming, crying, fainting, and stage-shoving at Osmond Brothers concerts, as opposed to his older brothers Wayne or Merrill. "He was the reason by the way that young girls screamed and cried and fainted and shoved themselves up against the stage at Osmond Brothers Concerts. They were not screaming for Wayne or for Merrill."

srcs.episode: Ep. 30 - The Sweet Sound of 70s Bubblegum Music

podcast.title: Dislike of Bubblegum Label
podcast.body: While the Osmonds as a group disliked the bubblegum label and preferred to be seen as rock artists, Donnie himself epitomized the bubblegum artist image, even as he tried to shed it later in his career without resorting to David Cassidy's more extreme methods. "Now the Osmonds did not like the bubblegum label they didn't. They wanted to be considered rock. And Donnie did his best to knock down that bubble gum image without going the way of David Cassidy as he got older. But look pop music fans especially the young ones they sure did love them as bubble gum idols especially of course Donnie."

srcs.episode: Ep. 30 - The Sweet Sound of 70s Bubblegum Music

podcast.title: Perfect Bubblegummer
podcast.body: Donnie Osmond was considered the "perfect bubblegummer" due to his cute, wholesome, and non-threatening image, making him an ideal teen idol for young female fans. "So Donnie Osmond was the perfect bubblegummer. He was cute and wholesome and totally not threatening."

srcs.episode: Ep. 30 - The Sweet Sound of 70s Bubblegum Music

podcast.title: Record Label Priority over Beastie Boys
podcast.body: The president of the Beastie Boys' record label reportedly told Adam Yauch that they couldn't afford to promote *Paul's Boutique* further because "they had a new, donny, osman record coming out," illustrating a perceived lack of faith in the Beastie Boys' album at the time. "Adam Yach remember as being told by the president of their label that they couldn't afford to sink any more money into promoting the album because, wow, they had a new, donny, osman record coming out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Record Label Priority over Beastie Boys
podcast.body: A new record by Donny Osmond was prioritized by the Beastie Boys' record label president over continued promotion for their "Paul's Boutique" album due to its poor sales. "they had a new, donny, osman record coming out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Solo Career Transition
podcast.body: It was deemed inevitable that Donnie would become a solo act given his overwhelming popularity and teen idol status within The Osmonds. "It was just a matter of time before Donnie became a solo act and what else were you going to do with a kid like that?"
